title: Compose async middleware
summary: Chain middleware functions that each receive a context and a next() function, with code that runs on the way in and out.
prompt:
Finish `compose(middleware)`. It returns `(ctx) => Promise<void>` that runs the list in order. Each middleware is `(ctx, next) => Promise<void> | void`; calling `await next()` runs the rest of the chain and resumes afterwards, so code after it runs on the way back out.

Rules:
- A middleware that does not call `next` ends the chain there.
- Calling `next()` twice in one middleware rejects with an `Error` containing `next() called multiple times`.
- A thrown error or rejection anywhere rejects the returned promise, and an earlier middleware can catch it with `try { await next() } catch {}`.
hints: Write a recursive `dispatch(i)` that calls `middleware[i](ctx, () => dispatch(i + 1))`.
Track the highest index dispatched so far; if `i <= index`, `next` was called twice.
Wrap the call in `Promise.resolve(...)` inside `try`, and return `Promise.reject(error)` from `catch`, so sync throws become rejections.
